questions.question: Consider the following [latex]B^+[/latex] tree with 5 nodes, in which a node can store at most 3 key values. The value 23 is now inserted in the [latex]B^+[/latex] tree. Which of the following options(s) is/are CORRECT?

options.A: None of the nodes will split.
options.B: At least one node will split and redistribute.
options.C: The total number of nodes will remain same.
options.D: The height of the tree will increase.

questions.explanation:
Inserting a new key into a [latex]B^+[/latex] tree always follows the same pattern: search down to the correct leaf, insert the key there in sorted order, and if that leaf now holds more than the maximum allowed keys (here, more than [latex]3[/latex]), it must split into two leaves, pushing/copying up a separator key into the parent.

Since the target leaf here is already at its maximum capacity of [latex]3[/latex] keys before inserting [latex]23[/latex], it overflows and must split; this new separator key then gets inserted into the parent node, which can itself overflow and split further, potentially propagating all the way up to a new root. Whenever a split reaches (or creates a new) root, the height of the tree increases by one level. Splitting always increases the total node count (a leaf becomes two, or an internal node splits into two) — it never leaves the count unchanged, and "no node splits" is only possible if the target leaf had spare capacity, which it did not here.

Answer: At least one node will split and redistribute; and the height of the tree will increase.

The value of |A-B| is _____________

Complete binary tree with 7 nodes: root, its two children L and R, and four grandchildren.
- BFS first 3: root, L, R [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] A = {root, L, R}
- DFS first 3: root, L, L's left child [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] B = {root, L, LL}

A [latex]-[/latex] B = {R} [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] |A [latex]-[/latex] B| = 1

Answer: 1

questions.question: The height of any rooted tree is defined as the maximum number of edges in the path from the root node to any leaf node. Suppose a Min-Heap [latex]T[/latex] stores 32 keys. The height of [latex]T[/latex] is _____________. (Answer in integer)
questions.explanation:
A min-heap with [latex]N[/latex] keys is stored as a nearly-complete binary tree, and its height (max edges from root to a leaf) is [latex]\lfloor\log_2N\rfloor[/latex].

Level [latex]0[/latex] holds [latex]1[/latex] node, level [latex]1[/latex] holds [latex]2[/latex], level [latex]2[/latex] holds [latex]4[/latex], level [latex]3[/latex] holds [latex]8[/latex], level [latex]4[/latex] holds [latex]16[/latex] — cumulatively [latex]1+2+4+8+16=31[/latex] nodes fill levels [latex]0[/latex] through [latex]4[/latex] completely. The [latex]32[/latex]nd key must then start a new level, level 5.

Answer: 5

questions.question: A queue is implemented using an array such that ENQUEUE and DEQUEUE operations are performed efficiently. Which one of the following statements is CORRECT (n refers to the number of items in the queue)?

options.A: Both operations can be performed in O(1) time
options.B:
At most one operation can be performed in O(1) time but the worst case time for
the other operation will be [latex]\Omega[/latex](n)
options.C: The worst case time complexity for both operations will be [latex]\Omega[/latex](n)
options.D: Worst case time complexity for both operations will be [latex]\Omega[/latex](logn)

questions.explanation:
Use a circular array with front and rear indices: ENQUEUE writes at rear and moves it, DEQUEUE reads at front and moves it (both modulo the array size). No shifting is needed, so both are [latex]O(1)[/latex].

Answer: Both operations can be performed in O(1) time

Assume that the table size is 23. Then the address returned by probe 1 in the probe sequence (assume that the probe sequence begins at probe 0) for key value k=90 is_____________.

Checking each statement:
- [latex]h_1(90)=90\bmod23=21[/latex]
- [latex]h_2(90)=1+(90\bmod19)=1+14=15[/latex]

Probe i = [latex](h_1+i\cdot h_2)\bmod23[/latex]. Probe 1 = [latex](21+15)\bmod23=36\bmod23=13[/latex]

Answer: 13

5. [latex]\text{printf("\%d", i)}[/latex] refers to the (unshadowed, outer) parameter [latex]i[/latex], which is still [latex]9[/latex].

questions.question:
Let A be a priority queue for maintaining a set of elements. Suppose A is implemented using a max-heap data structure. The operation Extract-Max(A) extracts and deletes the maximum element from A. The operation Insert(A,key) inserts a new element key in A. The properties of a max-heap are preserved at the end of each of these operations.
When A contains n elements, which one of the following statements about the worst case running time of these two operations is TRUE?

options.A: Both Extract-Max(A) and Insert(A,key) run in O(1).
options.B: Both Extract-Max(A) and Insert(A,key) run in O(log(n)).
options.C: Extract-Max(A) runs in O(1) whereas Insert(A,key) runs in O(n).
options.D: Extract-Max(A) runs in O(1) whereas Insert(A,key) runs in O(log(n)).

questions.explanation:
A heap of n elements has height about log n:
- Extract-Max: remove the root, move the last element to the root, and heapify down the height of the tree [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]O(\log n)[/latex].
- Insert: add at the end and bubble up to the root [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]O(\log n)[/latex].

Answer: Both run in O(log(n))

questions.question:
Consider a stack [latex]S[/latex] and a queue [latex]Q[/latex]. Both of them are initially empty and have the capacity to store ten elements each. The elements [latex]1,2,3,4[/latex], and [latex]5[/latex] arrive one by one, in that order. When an element arrives, it is assigned either to [latex]S[/latex] (pushed on [latex]S[/latex] ) or to [latex]Q[/latex] (enqueued to [latex]Q[/latex] ). Once all the five elements are stored, the output is generated in two steps. First, stack S is emptied by popping all elements. Then queue [latex]Q[/latex] is emptied by dequeueing all elements. The output obtained by following this process is [latex]\text{4 3 1 2 5}[/latex].

Given the output, the objective is to predict whether an element was assigned to [latex]S[/latex] or [latex]Q[/latex].

Which of the following options is/are possible valid assignment(s) of the elements?
Note: In the options, the notation [latex]x S[/latex] denotes that element [latex]x[/latex] was assigned to [latex]S[/latex] and [latex]y Q[/latex] denotes that element [latex]y[/latex] was assigned to [latex]Q[/latex].
questions.explanation:
The final output is: stack-popped elements first (in reverse of their push order), followed by queue-dequeued elements (in the same order they were enqueued). Target output: [latex]4,3,1,2,5[/latex].

Check each candidate by splitting into an [latex]S[/latex]-subsequence (in arrival order, then reversed for popping) and a [latex]Q[/latex]-subsequence (in arrival order, kept as-is):

- 1S,2Q,3S,4S,5Q: [latex]S[/latex] pushed in order [latex]1,3,4[/latex] → popped as [latex]4,3,1[/latex]. [latex]Q[/latex]: [latex]2,5[/latex]. Combined: [latex]4,3,1,2,5[/latex] — matches!
- 1Q,2Q,3S,4S,5Q: [latex]S[/latex] pushed [latex]3,4[/latex] → popped [latex]4,3[/latex]. [latex]Q[/latex]: [latex]1,2,5[/latex]. Combined: [latex]4,3,1,2,5[/latex] — matches!
- 1Q,2Q,3Q,4S,5S: [latex]S[/latex] pushed [latex]4,5[/latex] → popped [latex]5,4[/latex]. [latex]Q[/latex]: [latex]1,2,3[/latex]. Combined: [latex]5,4,1,2,3[/latex] — does not match.
- 1S,2S,3S,4Q,5Q: [latex]S[/latex] pushed [latex]1,2,3[/latex] → popped [latex]3,2,1[/latex]. [latex]Q[/latex]: [latex]4,5[/latex]. Combined: [latex]3,2,1,4,5[/latex] — does not match.

Answer: "1S,2Q,3S,4S,5Q" and "1Q,2Q,3S,4S,5Q" are both valid assignments.
